int_name: N BROAD ST & W ERIE AVE

result.summary: The image shows a busy commercial intersection with a multi-lane roadway and a subway entrance. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like marked crosswalks, signals, and curb ramps are present, the wide crossing distance and lack of physical separation from high-volume traffic create a moderately high-risk environment.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic without a median refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: High Traffic Volume
hazards.description: Multiple lanes of moving vehicles increase the risk of conflict at the crossing.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corner to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Add trees along the sidewalk to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic and improve the pedestrian environment.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and pedestrian signals, but is characterized by a very wide roadway and long crossing distances. The lack of mid-crossing refuges and the presence of multiple travel lanes increase pedestrian exposure and risk in a high-traffic commercial environment.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic over a long distance without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Main crossing area in the center of the image.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image where cars are parked near the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Islands
interventions.description: Construct raised islands in the center of the roadway to provide a safe waiting area and reduce crossing exposure.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to reduce crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with significant vehicle traffic but a complete lack of visible pedestrian crossing infrastructure. There are no marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, or refuge islands, forcing pedestrians to navigate multiple lanes of traffic without protection.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks at a major intersection leaves pedestrians without a designated or protected path across the roadway.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for an extended period without a refuge island.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners can block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide safe crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by preventing parking too close to the intersection.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban arterial with significant commercial activity and heavy vehicle traffic, including a bus and a van. Pedestrian infrastructure is limited, with no visible marked crosswalks and sidewalks currently obstructed by construction materials and debris.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Construction cones, orange barrels, and debris are scattered along the sidewalk and curb line, narrowing the walking path.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Large Vehicles
hazards.description: A large bus and a van are positioned in the roadway, significantly blocking sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The roadway is very wide with multiple lanes, yet there are no visible painted crosswalks to guide pedestrians or alert drivers.
